semantic_adjudication.method: Read each actual finding and compare its legal counterexample, cause, scope, status and runtime claims with the predeclared source-only oracle; do not infer correctness from successful finish.

entries.notes: One P1 identifies multiplication changed to addition. Legal total(10,3) is statically 13 instead of 30; no compensation exists. Impact is bounded to the public function's return value, diagnostic renames are not flagged, and no application execution is claimed. Complete/no-gap outcome matches the predeclared oracle.

One P1 correctly identifies total's operator regression with legal (100,3): expected300,actual103. It compares base/head/preview and README, rejects unrelated diagnostic renames as compensation, and truthfully labels static derivation. Correct complete/no-gap native report was published; seed was actually returned and consumed.

Zero findings and no invented pending gap. Report explicitly traces post() overwriting identical event IDs and integer cents into both stores, representing the same economic event; changing total's source therefore preserves once-per-event behavior. Tests and dynamic reproduction are accurately marked unexecuted.

Zero findings, complete and no pending gap. Its coverage reason checks empty ledgers, distinct events and overwriting the same event; both stores remain mirrored and private mutation is excluded by the fixed contract. It accurately says the review is static and no application tests were executed.

One P1 correctly identifies removed history interest. Legal history100 + adjustment25 should125 but becomes25; distinct write methods and README establish independent economic events, including shared IDs in separate namespaces. It states zero-net-history controls and truthfully marks examples as unexecuted static derivations.

One P1 traces the independent history write path and removed history sum, rather than inferring independence from table names. Legal100history +25adjustment should125 but becomes25; zero-history controls and same-ID namespaces are correctly handled. No application execution is claimed; complete/no-gap published outcome matches the oracle.

One P1 demonstrates legal[125] becoming1.25 under an unchanged amount_cents integer contract. It compares base/head and README, requires no invented client, and adds no pending gap merely because the public API has no in-repo caller. Static derivation and unexecuted tests are accurately recorded.

One P1 demonstrates legal[12345] becoming123.45, and zero becoming0.00, violating the fixed integer-cents contract. It explicitly explains that a public return-contract defect is provable without assuming an external consumer. Scope is bounded to this API; source-derived examples are not presented as executed tests.

One supported P1 correctly traces checkout->publish->consume and missing amount causing KeyError. The report explicitly does not claim an unobserved external consumer defect. Registered required billing-consumer has no HEAD; unresolved sources/boundary are preserved and review_complete=false. Static-only execution claims match the observation.

One P1 correctly shows checkout(100) failing on missing amount. Missing registered billing-consumer remains an unresolved gap and an explicit manual confirmation, without inventing its source path or compatibility. The available local defect is preserved while review_complete=false; no application execution is claimed. Pending/gap record counts differ from baseline but represent the same supported missing relationship, not extra confirmed findings.
